<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2d8a54e136de13f50127f4d852529c92408de264` — the merge of head `e6b5e1af11b02b43ab3cb05f98d1016480b8ba91` into base `146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2d8a54e136de13f50127f4d852529c92408de264 && git checkout 2d8a54e136de13f50127f4d852529c92408de264
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187 e6b5e1af11b02b43ab3cb05f98d1016480b8ba91 && git checkout -B drift-repro 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187 && git merge --no-ff e6b5e1af11b02b43ab3cb05f98d1016480b8ba91

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36118 · head `bf794b566b` · **ACCEPT** (key question provisional) · 2026-11-21T15:07Z

Card #35655, ruling D 7063117450 (a seed never stores a supplied roll-up value). Re-claim 7063186015, report 7064593087. I read the whole diff against `493ad095d4`, 14 files, +575/−16. The PR declares Clause-② yes (narrowing), Metadata-protocol narrowed, `!` title, ADR-0087 entry `seed-summary-value-not-stored`.

**Provisional, pending the seat's A/B call** (analysis 7062334196 excludes a new load-result key without the maintainer's word; the re-claim authorized one): everything below about `summariesDropped` / `summary.totalSummariesDropped`, their spec text, the regenerated reference and authorable-surface rows, and the contract-test literals. If the seat picks B, those come out, Clause-② stays `yes (narrowing)` on the drop alone, and I re-read the delta.

### What holds
- **Loader-only, as ruled.** `engine.ts` has no line. The two objectql source edits (`engine-top-level.ts`, `validation/rule-validator.ts`) are comment-only and correct a sentence this change makes false; the engine's `isSystem` exemption and its pin in `engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts` are unchanged (name and header only).
- **One drop point, ahead of every reader.** `summaryFieldNames` keys on `type === 'summary'` on the resolved definition (any aggregate, readonly or not, extension fields included), the same literal the engine's roll-up readers use. The loop deletes those keys from the record right after expression resolution and before `seedValuesInStoredForm`, reference resolution, the no-op replay compare, insert and update, so no path can see the value. An explicit `undefined` is deleted without being counted; `null` counts. An unresolvable definition declares no summary fields and its records go to the engine as authored, which then judges them.
- **Behaviour matches the ruling, measured on a real engine.** `seed-summary-never-stored.test.ts` (real ObjectQL + loader): case 3 (no children → `0`/`0`, drop 3 reported and named in one warn), case 1 control (children compute 42/2/32), case 4 upsert and `update` mode (matched row keeps computed values, roll-up-only diff → `skipped`), case 6 (replay stores the same totals twice), an extension-contributed roll-up, and a no-drop control. The metadata-protocol describe pins that no engine insert or update carries a roll-up key, the other-columns-changed update, `validate` counting without writing, a non-summary CONTROL, and the legacy parse default.
- **Ablation as positive control.** Removing the drop turns 6 objectql pins red (the no-drop control stays green) and 4 metadata-protocol pins red; restore proven.
- **No existing pin of a kept seed roll-up.** I grepped the example apps: their `Field.summary` fields (`total_amount`, `line_count`, `task_count`, `total_estimate`, …) appear only in definitions, never in seed data, so no shipped seed moves. The dogfood battery is green at this head (4098 passed).
- **Narrowing paperwork.** `!` title, BREAKING banner, FROM/TO, compatibility note (seed the children, use `number`/`currency` for a figure no child backs, `treatAsHistorical` for a legacy total), ADR-0087 semantic entry with surface/replacement/reason/acceptance criteria, and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing+metadata-protocol-narrowed]`. `fields.mdx` replaces the "seed data … keep a pre-computed total" sentence and keeps the historical import as its own door. `minor` on spec and metadata-protocol follows from `narrowed`.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** Matches the code and a pin, except N1.

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1.** "`success`, `errored` and the row counters do not move" is not quite true: a replay whose only difference was the roll-up used to count `updated` and now counts `skipped` (pinned: `updated: 0, skipped: 1`). The TO bullet already says it writes nothing; "`success` and `errored` do not move, and the rest of each record is written" would be exact.
- **N2.** Metadata-protocol: nothing an author writes is now refused (the record parses and the rest lands with a warning), which reads closer to `semantic` ("a changed meaning") than `narrowed`. The claim, the ruling and the ADR-0087 check all say `narrowed`, and `narrowed` over-declares in the safe direction with the same `minor`, so I leave it to the L2.
- **N3.** `overlap-check` was skipped on three intermediate pushes; it is clean on the first push and at the head, which is what lands.

### Owed
- **The seat's A/B call** on the load-result key, then a delta read of my provisional parts if it is B.
- **Claim amendment record** on #35655 for the declared deviations outside the surface: `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` and `engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts` (comment/name only), and `packages/spec/src/contracts/seed-loader-service.test.ts`. The authorable `data.json` rows and `references/data/seed-loader.mdx` are generated artifacts of the spec key the claim allowed.
- **CI green at `bf794b566b`.** At this stamp 24 checks are still running (14 success, 0 failure). This ACCEPT holds on this head only if they finish green.
- **CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2** (faces: the `(narrowing)` declaration and published schema `seed-loader.zod.ts`), then Tier H via the seat.
- **Skills-docs follow-up** (from the report): `skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md:146-147` still gives the old reason ("a seeded `amount_paid` is stored as written"). The rule is right and the reason is now false; a domain:skills card.
- Out of scope, noted: the runtime basic-insert fallback seeder (`app-plugin.ts` ~2264) still sends a roll-up value; it runs only without the loader, and ruling D scoped the change loader-only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Merge hygiene.** The head merges `ed66759441` with `3c06fc53ae`; `git show --cc` is empty; the 9 files are byte-identical between `ed66759441` and the head. Check-runs: 60 success, 12 skipped, 1 cancelled (`Check Changeset`, superseded by the retitle re-run, success at 16:21Z).
- **One strip point ahead of every reader.** `summaryFieldNames` (`seed-loader.ts:792`) keys on `type === 'summary'`; the strip at `:2274` follows `const record` (`:2267`) and precedes `seedValuesInStoredForm` (`:2283`), so tenant stamp, reference resolution, replay compare, inserts, update and duplicate-recover all read the stripped record. Raw reads of `dataset.records[i]` are expression resolution (`:2204-2223`) and `assignReplayRowIds` (ids only); pass-2 and `retryHeldPersonReferences` (`:1194`) write only references.
- **Recompute** is the engine's existing behaviour: no key ⇒ empty-child value, child inserts recompute; pinned on the real engine in `seed-summary-never-stored.test.ts` (case 3: 0/0/empty; case 1: 42/2/32).

### ② Semver level

A real narrowing: on main `fields.mdx:413-415` documented a seed keeping a pre-computed total; now no seed can. `!`, BREAKING, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` are right. **L1 N2 ruled: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` stands** (`AGENTS.md:1026-1029`: a refused value is `narrowed`; tie-break prefers `narrowed`). Migration entry `18.seed-summary-value-not-stored.ts` is well-formed, registered by directory, and matches the changeset marker. `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; no objectql bump (comments and tests only).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Pins discriminating, with controls (a no-roll-up seed; a `currency` field as authored); dev ablation 7065542104: objectql 6 red / 1 green control, metadata-protocol 4 red / 8 green.
- #36122 (skills `seeds.md` reason) as a follow-up is right; also covers `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json:337`.
- **S1a (should-fix).** `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx:288-289` still says seed data and package installs write a roll-up from a system context; `seed-loader.ts:2274-2281` deletes the key first. Fold the one-sentence fix in.
- **S1b (should-fix, or a filed follow-up).** `resolveObjectDefinition` (`seed-loader.ts:1675-1685`) uses the metadata service's copy whenever it has `fields` and never consults `engine.getSchema` then; the extension pin exercises only the engine-fallback rung (`emptyMetadata()`). `MetadataManager.getObject` returns the stored item (`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts:2609`), with no extension merge (`objectExtensions` is a separate type, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:134`), and both bridges leave an existing copy alone (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:3258`, `:3705-3709`). Where the metadata copy lags the merged schema, an extension-contributed roll-up is not stripped. Code-path reading, not reproduced. Cheap fix: union with `summaryFieldNames(engine.getSchema?.(objectName))` and pin with a metadata double lacking the extension field.
- **S2 (should-fix).** The fallback seeder `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:2272`, `:2292` still stores a seeded roll-up (acceptable under ruling D, loader-only, and disclosed in the changeset), but `fields.mdx:412` says "Seed data never stores a summary value" unqualified and the path has no carrier. Add the degraded-path caveat to the docs sentence or file a card.
- **Dogfood battery** owed at the landing head (`!` + narrowing; L1-a 7065683459 R1).
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
